latest_release.name: v1.13.0
latest_release.body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> This release drops support for Node 20, which is end-of-life. Self-hosters building from source now need Node 22.23.5, 24.22.3 or 26.13.1 and above for the latest security patches. The Docker image is updated to Node 26.13.1.

## What's Changed

This release upgrades the power of Search, adds a Gitea / Forgejo integration, expiry dates for public share links, and preview cards for links, alongside more MCP and OAuth spec compliance, security hardening, and continued performance work on the server.

### Highlights

* Added a Gitea / Forgejo integration in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14336
* Public share links can now have an expiry date in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14513 (Set a default expiry date at workspace level in the licensed edition)
* Links, documents, and collections can now be displayed as preview cards in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14511
* A destination can now be selected when importing in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14486
* Search filters have been redesigned and improved in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14589
* Settings now save automatically, and the settings layout has been tidied in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14569
* Menu items can now be filtered by typing in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14534

### MCP

* ChatGPT client metadata documents are now accepted for MCP OAuth in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14305
* Added `OAUTH_DISABLE_CIMD` to fall back to dynamic client registration in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14410 if your installation is unable to retrieve the CIMD due to network restrictions.
* OAuth discovery metadata now aligns with RFC 8414 and RFC 9728, and advertises missing fields in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14324 https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14315
* The token endpoint now returns standard OAuth error codes in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14312
* Dynamic client registration now returns `invalid_redirect_uri` in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14316
* API 401 responses now include a `WWW-Authenticate` header in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14321
* Every MCP tool annotation hint is now set explicitly, and `move_document` is marked as destructive in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14263 https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14320
* MCP endpoint request validation has been tightened in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14314
* Hop-by-hop headers from MCP SDK responses are no longer forwarded in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14335

### Performance improvements

* Reduced memory of the primary and worker processes in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14369
* Share page chunks are now loaded before the first render in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14322
* Share page content now renders without the export lock and is cached in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14284
* Mention suggestions are faster in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14583
* Locale files are smaller, with fewer locale fetches in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14592
* `documents.viewed` is faster for users with many views in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14430
* `views.list` is now paginated with a default limit of 100 in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14278
* Attachment `lastAccessedAt` writes are now throttled in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14276
* `lastActiveAt` writes from collaboration edits are now throttled in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14281
* Only ids are now loaded when resolving membership user ids in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14275
* Comment replies are now deleted in one statement, and `parentCommentId` is indexed in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14277
* The loaded collection is now kept when the document title changes in https://github.com/outline/outline/pull/14283
* Sourced member

detail.readme:
A fast, collaborative, knowledge base for your team built using React and Node.js.
Try out Outline using our hosted version at www.getoutline.com.

This is the source code that runs [**Outline**](https://www.getoutline.com) and all the associated services. If you want to use Outline then you don't need to run this code, A hosted version of the app is offered at [getoutline.com](https://www.getoutline.com). You can also find documentation on using Outline in [our guide](https://docs.getoutline.com/s/guide). If you'd like to run your own copy of Outline then this is the place for you. # Installation Please see the [documentation](https://docs.getoutline.com/s/hosting/) for running your own copy of Outline in a production configuration. Available container images: * [![Container Image Release](https://img.shields.io/docker/v/outlinewiki/outline?sort=semver&label=Latest%20release)](https://hub.docker.com/r/outlinewiki/outline) * [![Container Image Nightly](https://img.shields.io/docker/v/outlinewiki/outline?sort=date&label=Latest%20development%20version)](https://hub.docker.com/r/outlinewiki/outline) If you have questions or improvements for the docs please create a thread in [GitHub discussions](https://github.com/outline/outline/discussions). # Translation Outline is localized through community contributions on [CrowdIn](https://translate.getoutline.com/project/outline). See the [translation guide](docs/TRANSLATION.md) to help bring Outline to other languages. # Development There is a short guide for [setting up a development environment](https://docs.getoutline.com/s/hosting/doc/local-development-5hEhFRXow7). ## Architecture If you're interested in learning more about the Outline codebase please refer to the [architecture document](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) first for a high level overview of how the application is put together. ## Debugging In development Outline outputs simple logging to the console, prefixed by categories. In production it outputs JSON logs, these can be easily parsed by your preferred log ingestion pipeline. HTTP logging is disabled by default, but can be enabled by setting the `DEBUG=http` environment variable. logging can be enabled for all categories by setting `DEBUG=*` or for specific categories such as `DEBUG=database` and `LOG_LEVEL=debug`, or `LOG_LEVEL=silly` for very verbose logging. ## Tests We aim to have sufficient test coverage for critical parts of the application and aren't aiming for 100% unit test coverage. All API endpoints and anything authentication related should be thoroughly tested. To add new tests, write your tests with [Vitest](https://vitest.dev/) and add a file with `.test.ts` extension next to the tested code. ```shell # To run all tests make test # To run backend tests in watch mode make watch ``` Once the test database is created with `make test` you may individually run frontend and backend tests directly with vitest: ```shell # To run backend tests yarn test:server # To run a specific backend test in watch mode yarn test path/to/file.test.ts --watch # To run frontend tests yarn test:app ``` ## Migrations Sequelize is used to create and run migrations, for example: ```shell yarn db:create-migration --name my-migration yarn db:migrate yarn db:rollback ``` Or, to run migrations on test database: ```shell yarn db:migrate --env test ``` # License Outline is [BSL 1.1 licensed](LICENSE).
